before: CELIA. Why shouldn't I? Doesn't he deserve to be hated?
after: CELIA. Why shouldn't I? Doesn’t he deserve better?

before: DUKE SENIOR. Now, my comrades and brothers in exile, Hasn't long custom made this life sweeter Than that of painted pomp? Aren't these woods More free from peril than the envious court? Here we don't feel Adam's punishment, The difference of the seasons—when the icy fang And churlish chiding of the winter wind Bite and blow upon my body, Even till I shrink with cold, I smile and say 'This is no flattery; these are counsellors That feelingly persuade me of what I am.' Sweet are the uses of adversity, Which, like the toad—ugly and venomous— Still wears a precious jewel in its head; And this life of ours, free from public haunt, Finds tongues in trees, books in running brooks, Sermons in stones, and good in everything. I would not change it.

before: ROSALIND. Your accent is somewhat finer than you could have acquired in such a remote dwelling.
after: ORLANDO. Your accent is somewhat finer than you could have acquired in such a remote dwelling.

before: TOUCHSTONE. God reward you, sir; I wish the same for you. I push my way in here, sir, among the rest of the country couples, to swear vows and break them, as marriage binds and desire breaks free. A poor, plain-looking girl, sir, but she's my own; a strange whim of mine, sir, to claim for myself what another man would otherwise take. True honesty lives like a miser, sir, hidden away in a humble house — the way a pearl hides inside a homely oyster.
